extracted.intended_audience: educators, curriculum planners, and educational theorists
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and principles for judging the educational value of individual studies and for organizing a curriculum so that subjects contribute both intrinsically and instrumentally to a rich life of experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appreciation (Intrinsic) Value
rubrics_metrics.description: A study ought to have ultimate significance as an end in itself — to be appreciated, enjoyable, and a full experience for the student.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text emphasizes that every study in some aspect ought to be 'a good to be appreciated on its own account.' Literature and the fine arts exemplify heightened appreciation but 'every subject at some phase of its development should possess ... an aesthetic quality.' Anti-pattern: teaching a subject solely as a means so that students never realize its intrinsic worth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrumental (Means) Value — Situationally Determined
rubrics_metrics.description: When a study is treated as a means to an end, its value must be judged relative to the specific situation and the end it serves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuation as means (instrumental value) requires comparison in relation to some third thing (a further end). Example: music may be preferred to food in a context where hearing music is rare and one is not hungry. Guidance: determine which study 'contributes' more to the situation rather than assuming fixed rankings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivating Value / Immediate Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Topics should either have an immediate, motivating appeal to the pupil or be presented so that their role as means to intrinsic goods is perceived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a topic makes an immediate appeal, no justification is necessary; if not, teaching should 'establish consciousness of connection' between the study and intrinsic goods (e.g., let the pupil discover arithmetic's utility through tasks tied to his interests). Anti-pattern: insisting on remote future utilities while ignoring present engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution to Immediate Intrinsic Values as the Ultimate Criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The worth of any instrumental or derived value is determined by its contribution to immediate intrinsic experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text states that 'contribution to immediate intrinsic values ... is the only criterion for determining the worth of instrumental and derived values in studies.' Thus instrumental utilities are justified only insofar as they enrich lived experience directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding Fixed Hierarchies of Studies
rubrics_metrics.description: It is futile to attempt to establish a fixed hierarchy ranking subjects from least to most valuable; intrinsic worth is context-dependent and often incomparable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author argues against arranging studies in an absolute order of worth because many studies have unique, irreplaceable functions and their worth may be intrinsic. Anti-pattern: rigid curricula that claim certain subjects are always 'higher' than others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-Based Attribution of Values (Do Not Assume Inherent Powers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Values ascribed to subjects should be taken as contingent results of how they are taught and whether they actually accomplish stated ends, not as innate powers of the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: statements that 'mathematics trains memory or imagination' are only true if those results are actually produced. Fault lies with teaching methods if values aren't realized, not with the subject itself. Avoid using value-claims as mere justifications without empirical support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration / Unity of Experience (Oppose Segregation of Values)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization of curriculum should promote unity and mutual reinforcement among different interests (art, science, politics, work, leisure) rather than segregating them into isolated pigeon-holes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text criticizes curricula built by 'gathering together various studies' each meant to satisfy a separate end, producing a conglomerate. Instead favor overlapping aims so subjects reinforce one another and avoid educational disintegration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Overcrowding and Specialization; Favor Reorganization
rubrics_metrics.description: When curricula become congested with inherited or sectional studies, the remedy is careful reorganization of aims and methods rather than simply adding more subjects or reverting to a narrower traditional set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The passage warns that adding another study to fix deficiencies usually worsens congestion. Effective remedy: inspect, criticize, and revise the curriculum to ensure it accomplishes purpose rather than relying on purely quantitative cuts or nostalgic restorations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum Selection Should Reflect Pupils' Lives, Not Only Adult Interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjects included in the course should be examined to ensure they serve the immediate lives and interests of pupils rather than mainly reflecting adult or outdated values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text notes curricula often represent the 'values of adults rather than those of children and youth' or of an earlier generation. Recommendation: continual critical outlook and survey to keep content relevant to present pupil needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of General Values Is Provisional — Prefer Concrete Realizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract classifications (health, wealth, culture, etc.) are useful for survey but are provisional summaries; standards of valuation are ultimately found in specific realized experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat such abstractions as ultimate standards; use them as elevated viewpoints to survey distribution and proportion of experiences, but ground judgments in concrete student experiences and tastes/habits of preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey Criteria: Five Useful Educational Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: When surveying curriculum aims, consider whether studies contribute to (a) executive competency/efficiency, (b) sociability, (c) aesthetic taste, (d) trained intellectual method, and (e) conscientiousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author lists these as 'useful criteria for survey, criticism, and better organization of existing methods and subject matter.' They are not ultimate values but practical points of view for organizing instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Response / Use as Proof of Value
rubrics_metrics.description: A pupil's active response to material is evidence that the subject possesses value in his life; actual engagement is the test of worth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text says 'his response to the material shows that the subject functions in his life.' Thus observed interest and use should weigh heavily in curricular decisions. Anti-pattern: insisting on abstract justifications when pupils already show genuine concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation Strategy When Appetite Is Lacking
rubrics_metrics.description: If pupils lack appetite for a subject or their motives are perverted, instruction should make consequences conscious so that instrumental value is grasped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: for a child whose appetite is perverted, 'conscious reference to results is indicated.' In pedagogical practice, this means showing clear links between study and desired outcomes when intrinsic motivation is absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education Should Reconcile Preparation for Labor with Cultivation of Leisure
rubrics_metrics.description: Educational aims must bridge useful labor and cultivated leisure so that training for work and for leisure mutually reinforce rather than form a class-based opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter traces historical segregation between liberal and practical education and argues for overlapping aims: education aiming at leisure should indirectly reinforce efficiency in work and vice versa. Anti-pattern: treating vocational training as inherently inferior or strictly separate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim of Education: Living Itself — Studies as Ingredients of a Fruitful Life
rubrics_metrics.description: Education is identical with operating the living of a life that is fruitful and inherently significant; studies are not mere means but ingredients of living itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This philosophical criterion shifts evaluation away from seeing education as mere preparation; curriculum planning should treat studies as contributing directly to the process of living, not solely subordinated to external ends.
